1.pericope_label: Command the children of Israel: this is the land that shall fall unto you

schools.summary: Calvin makes God a careful head of a household securing an unquestionable title, and traces the southern line himself; Gill turns the command into a duty of vigilance over the boundary.
Henry reads the survey as a legal grant rather than a map, and sets the described land against the larger promise reaching to the Euphrates.
Wesley finds in the limits a restraint on conquest and measures the smallness of the land against its fruitfulness; Clarke gives the chapter’s outline and refuses the geography.
Keil and Delitzsch identify the southern line with the boundary of Judah and weigh the Hebrew idiom for contact along a border.

debates.question: Why are the boundaries specified at all?

sides.position: As the terms of a grant, so that what is conveyed is certainly known
To secure a title that could never be called in question
To restrain them from enlarging their empire like other nations
So that they might know whom to dispossess and guard against encroachment

outliers.note: Sets the topography aside as useless in a commentary, referring the reader to a survey or a good map instead.

3.pericope_label: Your south border shall be the outmost coast of the salt sea

schools.summary: Gill fixes the direction of the line and the force of the verb for turning.
Wesley accounts for the windings, the name of the salt sea and the emphatic use of the sea, and locates Azmon; Clarke identifies the salt sea and reports two views of the river of Egypt.

Ellicott re-renders the opening clause, traces the line by the natural division between cultivation and desert, and identifies both Akrabbim and the brook of Egypt; Keil and Delitzsch carry the description on to the western sea.

debates.question: What is the river of Egypt that closes the southern line?

sides.position: The eastern branch of the Nile, or a river south of Philistia
The watercourse called Sihor, dividing Egypt from Canaan

outliers.note: Identifies the ascent of Akrabbim with a specific row of white cliffs crossing the Arabah some eight miles from the Dead Sea.

6.pericope_label: This shall be your north border

schools.summary: Gill locates the entrance of Hamath in the pass between the two Lebanon ranges and weighs an ancient identification of Ziphron with a town in Cilicia.

Clarke explains the epithet great from the single Hebrew word for any standing water; Wesley limits the stretch of coast in view and identifies Mount Hor with Libanus against the Hor where Aaron died.

Ellicott re-renders the western clause, canvasses the rival mountains and admits that Ziphron and Enan are unknown; Keil and Delitzsch declare the northern line undeterminable and distinguish two places named Riblah.

debates.question: Which mountain is the Hor of the northern border?

sides.position: Not Hermon, which stands too far east; some peak near the Mediterranean, or one of the Lebanon peaks visible from Sidon
Libanus, and certainly not the Hor where Aaron died
Undeterminable: only Hamath among these places is securely known

outliers.note: Turns a boundary clause into a lexical note, observing that one Hebrew word covers every standing water and that the Greek New Testament inherits the same imprecision.

10.pericope_label: Ye shall point out your east border; the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea

schools.summary: Gill identifies Shepham and the northern terminus, reports and rejects the identification of Riblah with the town in Hamath, and passes on the rabbinic idiom for a southward border.
Clarke gives the equivalents for the lake and turns the Jordan into a catalogue of the miracles wrought in it.
Ellicott fixes the fountain, distinguishes the two Riblahs, and traces the name of the lake; Keil and Delitzsch carry the description into the allotment.

debates.question: Is this Riblah the town in the land of Hamath?

sides.position: No — the fountain named beside it fixes a different site
The Targums identify it with Daphne near Antioch, but that carries the limits too far

outliers.note: Leaves the boundary line to recite the history of the Jordan, from the crossing on dry ground to the baptism of Christ.

13.pericope_label: This is the land which ye shall inherit by lot

schools.summary: Calvin denies that the trans-Jordan settlement amounted to exclusion from the promise and explains how the request enlarged the land; Gill identifies the tribes.
Clarke inventories the natural advantages of the land, its sheltering ranges, its water and its produce.
Keil and Delitzsch state the allotment and its exceptions; Ellicott corrects the rendering of the phrase describing where the two and a half tribes settled.

debates.question: What does the trans-Jordan settlement mean for the two and a half tribes?

sides.position: They are excluded from the lot only, not from the inheritance, and their request enlarged the land
They had simply received their portion already, and so had nothing to do with the division

outliers.note: Leaves the legal arrangement to describe the country itself, its shelter from desert and northern winds and the mines beneath it.

themes: the two and a half tribes

16.pericope_label: These are the names of the men which shall divide the land unto you

schools.summary: Calvin answers why judges were needed if the lot decided; Gill gives the arithmetic of the ten princes and weighs a rabbinic rendering.
Henry observes that commissioners are named before any general, since the land was to be won by God’s power, and reads Eleazar and Joshua as a figure of Christ dividing the heavenly inheritance.
Ellicott limits the lot to position rather than dimension and notes that only Caleb is named elsewhere; Keil and Delitzsch distinguish heads of fathers’ houses from heads of tribes.
Wesley sets out the office Eleazar was to discharge in casting the lots.

debates.question: If the land was divided by lot, why appoint commissioners at all?

sides.position: Because the dimensions had to answer to the numbers in each tribe; the lot fixed only which district fell to whom
To preside at the casting, settle disputes and see that all was done fairly

outliers.note: Reads the two chief commissioners typologically, as priest and king dividing a heavenly Canaan, while keeping the disposal with the Father.

19.pericope_label: And the names of the men are these

schools.summary: Gill notes that the men were nominated by God and not chosen by their tribes, which secures the impartiality of the division at its source.
Clarke shows that the list follows the geography of the settlement rather than any earlier order of the tribes, and traces it lot by lot; Wesley draws providence from the same fact.

debates.question: Why are the tribes listed in this order?

sides.position: Because it follows the order in which they afterwards possessed the land
The point of the list is rather that the men were named by God, not elected

outliers.note: Takes a list already fixed to the future map as proof of providence, since the order anticipates lots not yet cast.

29.pericope_label: These are they whom the Lord commanded to divide the inheritance

schools.summary: Gill reads the closing formula as a binding charge rather than a list, and notes that the order preceded the conquest and was executed at the sanctuary.

outliers.note: Treats the date of the order as itself an argument, since a command to divide a land not yet entered presupposes that the possession was certain.
